headline: Asia's data centre building hit a run of setbacks, with two share listings pulled and governments in Thailand and Indonesia pausing projects.
score_reason: Pool score 5 kept: a roundup read in full with several dated setbacks; most are reported by one outlet.
importance_line: Governments and investors across Asia are slowing the AI build-out over funding costs, approvals and power use, which affects local energy users and the companies that planned these sites, though the piece is a single outlet's roundup.
summary: Light Reading reports that Australian AI data centre firm Firmus withdrew its planned AU$7.1 billion share listing on Friday 9 Oct 2026 after investors balked at the price, and Philippine telecoms company PLDT put the listing of its data centre property trust off until 2027, blaming higher interest rates. It adds that Indonesia's West Java halted a 640-megawatt project for missing approvals, Thailand suspended 166 projects a month ago to write new rules, and Malaysia's energy regulator is reported to say demand growth has risen from 1.5 to 2 percent a year to nearly 10 percent because of data centres; our 9 Oct edition carried Reuters on Firmus shelving its listing.
notes: Follow-up on the Firmus part only (our 9 Oct edition item 10, Reuters); the PLDT, Indonesia, Thailand and Malaysia points are new in our reports. The Financial Times report on private funding of up to $3 billion is relayed by Light Reading.
